title: Inflation and Market Stress Across Bond Maturities

maps.specifics: Reported: 'impact of inflation, market stress on long term / short term bond'; 'climate risk and inflation.' The differential effect across the maturity spectrum, and the risk-premium and convexity contributions to term-structure shape, are the examinable mechanics.

selectors.name: Higher expected inflation: forwards and bond values
selectors.what: Higher expected inflation is higher expected short rates, so the expectations term D x E[dr]/dt of the forward rate rises, and its effect on forward rates and bond values grows with duration: long bonds are hit more than short bonds.
selectors.theory: Forward rate f(T) = r0 + D x E[dr]/dt + lambda x D - (1/2) x C x sigma^2: the higher the current short rate, the more rates are expected to rise and the greater the duration, the higher the forward rate. Long-run expectations can be anchored by macroeconomics (long-run real rate plus long-run inflation, for example 1% + 3% = 4%), and expectations cannot be separated from risk premium using the term structure alone.

selectors.name: Market stress: risk premium versus convexity
selectors.what: Market stress as a higher risk premium and higher rate volatility: the premium term lambda x D grows with duration and raises forward rates and expected returns, while the convexity term (1/2) x C x sigma^2 lowers long forward rates, so the two pull in opposite directions.
selectors.theory: Expected return of a risk-averse investor E[dP/P] = r0 dt + lambda x D dt (for example r = 1%, D = 5, lambda = 10 bp gives 1.5%); Sharpe ratio = lambda / sigma; return decomposition dP/P = f(T) dt - D dr + (1/2) x C x sigma^2 dt, with a rate rise costing return in proportion to duration and volatility adding return in proportion to convexity. Higher volatility lowers forward rates, more at long terms because C grows with term.

selectors.name: Climate shock as inflation and stress scenario
selectors.what: A climate-related shock framed as an inflation and market-stress scenario and asked about for short versus long bonds: treated through the expectations term (expected inflation), the convexity term (uncertainty and volatility) and the risk premium (required compensation), with the effect larger at long maturities.

notSelected: MR-13 c (Jensen's inequality and the convexity effect, Vardeez pointer only, drilled in D12), MR-15 d (CIR and lognormal short-rate models, drilled in D1) and IM-2 b (inflation, growth and volatility as macroeconomic factors for asset returns) carry no D18 shape, and the pure expectations versus pure risk premium hypotheses appear only in the revision notes, not in any shape or Map point.
